rationale: C12 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are personal Eisenhower letters praising an individual's exceptional contribution, stressing the burden or sacrifice involved, tying the work to a larger national objective, and expressing personal gratitude. The especially close phrasing around “deep appreciation,” “the contribution you have made,” and sustained personal effort is more concrete than generic commendation. C07 and C15 share the appreciation-for-demanding-service structure but have less distinctive verbal overlap.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I admire all the more the tremendous job you have done ... You have personally carried a back-breaking load of hard, tedious, day by day and state by state campaigning.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: My appreciation of the contribution you have made is enhanced by the fact that I have known something of the personal sacrifice you have made ... the many months involved went by
shared_material.explanation: Both emphasize that appreciation is heightened by knowledge of the recipient’s prolonged personal burden and sacrifice.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I can find no words to express my deep appreciation of the contribution you have made toward that goal.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I want to express again my deep appreciation of your outstanding contribution ... My appreciation of the contribution you have made is enhanced
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive cluster of shared language: “deep appreciation,” “contribution,” and “the contribution you have made.”

shared_material.child_excerpt: No man could have done more effective work than you to further that hope.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The conclusion of this agreement ... is due in significant measure to your expert knowledge ... persistence and ... skillful diplomacy.
shared_material.explanation: Each credits the recipient’s personal qualities and work as materially advancing a stated national objective.
